title: Common principal-open comparison cover for an open in a quasi-affine scheme
statement: Let $u:U\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $V$ isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, and let $r:B\to A$ be restriction. Let $j_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $j_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ correspond to identity ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and put $q=\operatorname{Spec}r$. For a global section $h$ on a scheme $X$, write $X_h=\{x:h_x\in\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\times}\}$. Then $j_V$ is an open immersion and $q\circ j_U=j_V\circ u$. Put $H=(j_V\circ u)(U)$ and $I=\{g\in B:D(g)\subseteq H\}$, where $D(g)=\{\mathfrak p:g\notin\mathfrak p\}$. The $D(g)$ for $g\in I$ cover the open subscheme $H$. For every $g\in I$, $V_g\subseteq u(U)$ is affine and $j_V$ induces an isomorphism $V_g\xrightarrow{\sim}D(g)$. With $f=r(g)$ one has $U_f=u^{-1}(V_g)$ and $q^{-1}(D(g))=D(f)$, and $u$ restricts to an isomorphism $U_f\xrightarrow{\sim}V_g$. The affine opens $U_{r(g)}$, $g\in I$, cover $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ARY, lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine, proof: common charts V_g = U_f and their coverage

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] to $V$: its stated quasi-affineness hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $V$, so $j_V$ is an open immersion. By the ring-map construction of $q=\operatorname{Spec}r$ in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], both maps $q\circ j_U$ and $j_V\circ u$ to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ induce the ring map $r:B\to A$ on sections: the first induces $\mathrm{id}_A\circ r$, and the second induces $r\circ\mathrm{id}_B$. Injectivity of the bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] gives $q\circ j_U=j_V\circ u$.

source.place: Tag 01P9, lemma-quasi-affine; Tag 0ARY, lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine, first proof sentence (using Schemes Tag 01I1)

proof.text: By [def-weil-open-immersion], $u$ identifies $U$ with the open subscheme $u(U)$ of $V$, and $j_V$ identifies $V$ with an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Thus $H=j_V(u(U))$ is open. For $z\in H$, clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] gives $g\in B$ with $z\in D(g)\subseteq H$. This $g$ belongs to $I$, and every $D(g)$ indexed by $I$ lies in $H$ by definition. Therefore these distinguished opens cover $H$.

source.place: Tag 0ARY, lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine, last sentence of proof; basis supplied by Algebra Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology (14)

proof.text: Fix $g\in I$. The preimage clause of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], applied to $j_V$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$, gives $V_g=j_V^{-1}(D(g))$. Since $D(g)\subseteq H\subseteq j_V(V)$, restricting the isomorphism of $V$ with its image from [def-weil-open-immersion] gives $V_g\simeq D(g)$, induced by $j_V$. Also $j_V^{-1}(H)=u(U)$ by injectivity of $j_V$, hence $V_g\subseteq u(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and [def-weil-open-immersion], $D(g)$ is isomorphic to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$. Composing gives $V_g\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B_g$, so $V_g$ is affine by [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Tag 0ARY, lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine, common charts; Schemes Tag 01I3, lemma-standard-open-affine

proof.text: Put $f=r(g)$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback] to $u$ gives $u^{-1}(V_g)=U_f$, because pullback of a global function under the open immersion is restriction. Applying the preimage clause of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] to $q=\operatorname{Spec}r$ gives $q^{-1}(D(g))=D(f)$: its corresponding ring map is $r$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the unit locus of $f\in A$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is its distinguished open $D(f)$.

source.place: Tag 0ARY, lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine, proof: f is the image of g and U_f = V_g; Schemes Tag 01I1 and Modules Tag 0H78

proof.text: Since $V_g\subseteq u(U)$, restrict the inverse of $u:U\simeq u(U)$ from [def-weil-open-immersion] to $V_g$. Its image lies in $U_f=u^{-1}(V_g)$ by step 4. The two composites with $u|_{U_f}$ are identities, being restrictions of the inverse identities for $u:U\simeq u(U)$. Thus $U_f\simeq V_g$, and step 3 gives $U_f\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B_g$, so $U_f$ is affine by [def-pc-scheme]. For $x\in U$, step 2 gives $g\in I$ with $j_V(u(x))\in D(g)$. Then $u(x)\in V_g$ and $x\in U_{r(g)}$ by steps 3 and 4. Hence the specified affine opens cover $U$.
